findings.issue: Spurious syllables きごう (the analyzer's label 記号 'symbol' for the space characters) leaked into the phonetic transcription twice. The kana teaches a wrong pronunciation of the sentence.
findings.current: ともだちときごうこーひーをきごうのむ
findings.suggested: ともだちとこーひーをのむ

findings.current: あしたからきごうなつやすみです
findings.suggested: あしたからなつやすみです

findings.issue: Same artifact as kana: 'kigou' inserted twice where the jp has spaces. This is beyond the known punctuation/katakana romaji issue — it adds nonexistent syllables.
Same artifact as kana: 'kigou' inserted where the jp has a space, adding nonexistent syllables (distinct from the known punctuation/katakana issue).
Whitespace token (s = " ") carries reading きごう — the tokenizer's POS label 記号 was stored as a reading. A space has no reading; this is the source of the kana/romaji corruption.
findings.suggested: (no reading — set to null/empty for whitespace token)

findings.issue: Second whitespace token also carries the bogus reading きごう (analyzer label 記号 stored as reading).
findings.suggested: (no reading — set to null/empty for whitespace token)

findings.issue: Generated JP uses 然うして, an archaic/literary kanji spelling essentially never used in modern Japanese; standard orthography is kana そうして (or そして). No native would write this in a normal N3-level sentence. Tokens/expl referencing 然う need the same fix.
findings.current: お金をためて、然うして車を買った
findings.suggested: お金をためて、そうして車を買った

findings.issue: Token order defect: the sub-tokens 土曜 + 日 (components of 土曜日) sit at the START of the token list, before 柔道, instead of immediately preceding their compound 土曜日 (the convention used elsewhere, e.g. ドイツ+製 before ドイツ製). A rendered dissection shows tokens out of sentence order.
findings.current: token list begins: 土曜, 日, 柔道, の, 試合, …
findings.suggested: …試合, は, 土曜, 日, 土曜日, に, ある (sub-tokens moved adjacent to 土曜日)

findings.issue: Garbled final clause: "in the sense of 'to happen, to take place' an event" is ungrammatical English (dangling 'an event').
findings.current: The verb ある ('to exist/be there') is used here in the sense of 'to happen, to take place' an event.
findings.suggested: The verb ある ('to exist/be there') is used here in the sense of an event 'happening / taking place'.

findings.issue: Same garbled ending in pt: "no sentido de 'acontecer, ter lugar' um evento" deixa 'um evento' solto e agramatical.
findings.current: O verbo ある ('existir/haver') é usado aqui no sentido de 'acontecer, ter lugar' um evento.
findings.suggested: O verbo ある ('existir/haver') é usado aqui no sentido de um evento 'acontecer, ter lugar'.

findings.issue: Truncated gloss: "('much', 'that')" — the second gloss was cut off (should be 'that much'); as written, "'that'" is confusing and does not match the pt version ('não... muito / não... tanto').
findings.current: The adverb あまり ('much', 'that') always appears with negation, creating the sense 'not... much'.
findings.suggested: The adverb あまり ('(not) much', '(not) that much') always appears with negation, creating the sense 'not... much'.

findings.issue: lit_en fails to mirror the topic structure 試合は…ある and diverges from lit_pt, which correctly mirrors it ('Quanto à competição de judô, no sábado, há/acontece'). As written it is just the natural translation, not the structural one.
findings.current: There is a judo competition on Saturday.
findings.suggested: As for the judo competition, on Saturday, there is / it takes place.
